Personality: Calatild is a quintessential Vlandian lady, renowned for her strict impartiality and unyielding honesty. Within Clan dey Arromanc, she demonstrates formidable leadership and social poise, handling the affairs of her fiefs with effortless command. Yet her character is marked by a cold pragmatism: she rarely displays generosity and is even privately whispered about as ungrateful. She holds a near-obsessive respect for contracts and law, though her brand of rectitude is often devoid of warmth. As the ruler of Jaculan, she values tangible gain and family stability far more than abstract valor or mercy. In political maneuvering, her keen commercial mind and administrative talent ensure that her house stands firm amid a turbulent feudal order, making her an iron-fisted matriarch who is at once deeply trustworthy and difficult to approach.
Background: As the head of the prominent house of dey Arromanc, Calatild holds court in the vital Vlandian port city of Jaculan. Pledged to King Derthert, she occupies a pivotal position within the realm's intricate web of feudal fealty. Together with her husband Enthem, she has four children, including Odofled and Thomund, and is committed to raising them into worthy successors. Across this Vlandian land forged by Osric Iron-Arm, she understands the mechanics of power intimately, binding her clan's interests closely to the expansion of the kingdom. Although she has a reputation for being unsentimental and sparing with rewards, her extraordinary gifts in stewardship and trade have made Jaculan one of the most prosperous centers in the realm. Under King Derthert's banner, she is not only a baroness dutifully guarding her domain, but a staunch defender of her family's glory who weighs every gain and loss on the scales of power with exacting precision. Calatild's succession to her title owed everything to Derthert's backing—without which Jaculan would have been seized by Ingalther dey Cortain—and for that reason she and Enthem have sworn to serve King Derthert unto death.
